result.title: Neuro-Inspired Inhibitory Message Passing for Accurate and Token-Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
result.summary: Multi-agent systems promise to solve problems by bringing together information beyond the reach of any individual agent. Retrieval and tool use can distribute this information across agents, making communication essential to collaboration. A central challenge is keeping crucial evidence visible in each agent's context as messages accumulate. Repeated information can crowd out rare, decisive evidence. Models of cortical circuits suggest a principle for addressing this imbalance: inhibition can selectively suppress shared inputs while preserving sensitivity to weaker signals. We adapt this principle into inhibitory message passing, a training-free communication router that cancels redundant evidence separately for each evidence sentence and receiver. Each round, it forwards evidence sentences restated in agents' messages, delivering each at most once to receivers whose own evidence lacks it and excluding the senders' reasoning and answers. Against standard message passing, accuracy in peer groups rose by 39-77 percentage points across three benchmarks, and tokens per run fell by 10-46%. Gains held across seven open models spanning four to thirty-two billion parameters and two commercial models, in groups up to sixty-four agents, and across multi-agent architectures including peer-to-peer, orchestrator-worker, and multilevel hierarchical organizations. These findings support a scalable design pattern for more accurate and token-efficient multi-agent reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出免训练的通信路由「inhibitory message passing」，仿皮层抑制原理，按证据句和接收者分别抵消冗余证据，仅在对方缺少该证据时至多转发一次并排除推理与答案，从而在多智能体群组中提升准确率并减少 token 消耗。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「抑制共享冗余、保留弱信号」的逐接收者证据路由，可能为 LVR 中被反复提到的视觉证据筛选与细节被淹没问题提供可核查的方法线索，但它处理的是文本多智能体消息，能否迁移到视觉 token 或 latent 状态尚待人工判断。
